name: Bacterial Chemotaxis and Signal Transduction
description: Bacterial chemotaxis is a sophisticated signal transduction system allowing E. coli to sense chemical gradients and bias flagellar rotation toward attractants and away from repellents. The system uses methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins (MCPs) as sensors, CheA-CheW as signal transduction complex, CheY as response regulator controlling flagellar motors, and CheR/CheB as adaptation enzymes providing sensory memory through receptor methylation. This demonstrates biological computation through phosphorylation cascades, temporal sensing, and adaptation.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on verified biochemical and structural data from decades of research on bacterial chemotaxis. The system is one of the best-understood signal transduction pathways in biology. All molecular components, phosphorylation cascades, and adaptation mechanisms have been validated against primary research sources including structural studies of receptor complexes.

notes: This flowchart represents bacterial chemotaxis with 61 unique nodes (A-BH + ANDGATE1). Contains 3 OR logic gates (attractant detection, repellent detection) and 1 AND gate (adaptation balance). Demonstrates sophisticated biological computation including phosphorylation cascades, sensory adaptation through methylation, temporal gradient sensing, and motor control. CheY-P acts as diffusible messenger between receptors and flagellar motors.
